module.name: Context Logic
module.description: The module describes the structure, function, and effect of context in the Behavioral Change Model (BCM) 2.0. Context is not an environment, but a structurally effective space in which utility effects can only be realized, inhibited, or changed.

A1.title: Module Metadata
A1.text: Module type: context_module_structural_space. Chapter ID: 8904. Epistemic class: operational. Linked standard: BCM3_02_AOM v2.2 (FA-STD-10061 §3.1–3.4). Registry version: 2.5. Author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Architecture Core. Meta reference: BCM2_00_STD9232 §2.1. Status: active. Validation rule: AOM-STRUC-01. Validation status: STRUCT_VALID_200. Last audit: 2025-10-24.

A2.title: Scope and Application
A2.text: Application domains: Architecture models with context dependency, simulations with context-sensitive dynamics, segmentations with context-modulated effects, derivation of intervention-capable ΔC(t) paths. Temporal scope: time-point-based and dynamic simulations (ΔC over t). Modularity: applicable in all BCM2 and BCM3 complementary modules. Restrictions: only initializable when Awareness (7240), Willingness (7243), and Segment Logic modules (7257) are active. Meta reference: BCM2_00_STD9232 §2.2. Status: active. Validation rule: AOM-SEM-01. Validation status: STRUCT_VALID_200.

A3.title: Purpose and Function
A3.text: Goals: Modeling of contextual structures (vectorial), assessment of segment-relational effects and context elasticity, integration of context axes in utility, awareness, and complementarity logic, calculation of context-modulated thresholds and reactions. Functional role: The module operationalizes the contextual effect level at which individual, collective, and identity utility functions are realized or inhibited. Outputs: φ(C⃗) – Context modulation function, χ(C⃗,S) – Context-dependent awareness probability, δ_i(C⃗) – Threshold shift through context, Ω(C,t) – Context dynamics over time. Linked axioms: AX_0.00c, AX_0.00e, AX_0.00j. Meta reference: BCM2_00_STD9232 §2.3. Status: active. Validation rule: AOM-EPI-01. Validation status: STRUCT_VALID_200.

A4.title: Binding Logic Rules (Axioms KX1–KX21)
A4.text: This section contains the formal axioms that define the binding logic rules for the Context Logic module. These axioms establish the foundational principles for context-dependent behavior modeling, including context structure, dynamics, complementarity, awareness, segmentation, thresholds, and organizational hierarchies.

axioms.title: Context is not utility, but structurally effective impact horizon
axioms.formula: U_i(t) = f(INU_i, KNU_i, IDN_i | C⃗(t), α_control, Bias(E1–E5)) with U_i ≠ C⃗(t) ∧ ∂U_i/∂C⃗ ≠ 0
axioms.description: Context influences behavior and utility realization, but is not itself a utility function. It forms the structural impact horizon in which utility functions only become effective or remain inhibited. Its effect varies over time, stability, and epistemic coherence.

axioms.title: Context acts mediated and structurally feedback-coupled
axioms.formula: V_i(t+1) = f(U_i(t), κ(C⃗,t), A_mod(C⃗,t), θ_i(C⃗,t), Ω(C⃗,t,α_control,ψ,Bias)) with ∂V_i/∂C⃗ ≠ 0
axioms.description: Context influences behavior through modulation functions such as complementarity, awareness, and decision thresholds, but simultaneously acts structurally back on behavior through the dynamic context function Ω(C⃗,t,α_control,ψ,Bias). This describes systemic drift, resonance, and stability damping between behavior and context over time.

axioms.title: Context is vectorial, multidimensional, structure-typed, and dynamically feedback-coupled
axioms.formula: C⃗(t) = { (c_i, w_i, τ_i(t), α_control_i, ψ_i(t), Bias_i(E1–E5)) | i = 1,…,n; Σw_i = 1 } ∧ dC⃗/dt ≠ 0
axioms.description: The context of a system is understood as a dynamic, vectorial space C⃗(t) consisting of multiple dimensions c_i. Each dimension represents an independent structural effect level (institutional, social, symbolic, technical, physical, media, etc.) and is modulated over time, resonance ψ(C⃗,t), stability α_control, and epistemic distortion Bias(E1–E5).

axioms.title: Complementarities are context-modulated, segment-relative, and dynamically feedback-coupled
axioms.formula: Comp(U_i,U_j|C⃗,t,S) = Comp₀(U_i,U_j)·φ(C⃗,t,S,ψ,Bias) + ε(Ω(C⃗,t),α_control) ∧ dComp/dt ≠ 0
axioms.description: The strength and direction of complementarities between utility functions U_i and U_j depend on the structure, dynamics, stability, and perception of context. Context axes C⃗(t) modulate the interaction through the function φ(C⃗,t,S,ψ,Bias). Resonance ψ(C⃗,t) and stability α_control determine whether complementarities are amplified, damped, or become unstable.

axioms.title: Awareness is context-dependent, dynamic, and segment-relational
axioms.formula: P(A=1 | C⃗,t,S) = χ(C⃗,t,S,α_control) = σ(β₀ + Σ β_i·C_i(t) + γ_S + δ·Ω(C⃗,t) - η·Bias(E1–E5))
axioms.description: The probability and intensity of awareness depends on the structure and dynamics of context as well as segment affiliation. Awareness emerges through resonance between context axes C⃗(t) and segment-relative perception filters ω_S.

axioms.title: Context acts segment-relationally and perception-differentiated
axioms.formula: V_i(S_a,t) = f(U_i, C⃗,t, ω_Sa, χ(C⃗,t,Sa), α_control, Bias(E1–E5)) ≠ V_i(S_b,t) = f(U_i, C⃗,t, ω_Sb, χ(C⃗,t,Sb), α_control, Bias(E1–E5)) for S_a ≠ S_b
axioms.description: Segments react differently to the same context because their internal perception functions ω_S and awareness profiles χ(C⃗,t,S) differ. Context effect is thus relational and dependent on segment-internal coherence, institutional stability (α_control), and perception bias (E1–E5).

axioms.title: Context dynamically and perception-dependently influences utility thresholds
axioms.formula: θ_i(C⃗,t) = θ₀i + δ_i(C⃗,t) - λ·χ(C⃗,t,S) + κ·(1 - α_control) + η·Bias(E1–E5)
axioms.description: The decision threshold θ_i of actor i is not a constant quantity but is modulated by the current context vector C⃗(t), individual awareness χ(C⃗,t,S), institutional stability (α_control), and perception bias (E1–E5).

axioms.title: Context is inertial, feedback-coupled, and dynamic
axioms.formula: C⃗(t+1) = C⃗(t) + ψ(C⃗,t,α_control)·[g(V_t) - h(C⃗(t)) + ξ·Bias(E1–E5)]
axioms.description: Context develops over time through feedback with behavior. Changes do not occur instantaneously but inertially and dependent on the resonance function ψ(C⃗,t), which describes sensitivity to behavior and institutional stability α_control.

axioms.title: There is no context-neutral state
axioms.formula: ∀ V ∈ Behavior : ∃ C ∈ Context with ∂V/∂C ≠ 0
axioms.description: Every observable behavior is under the influence of a context. A context-free state does not exist; every behavioral variation implies a change in at least one context dimension.

axioms.title: Context is only structurally changeable
axioms.formula: ΔC⃗ = Ω(C⃗,ΔI,α_control)·[f(ΔInstitutions,ΔRules,ΔNorms) + ξ·Bias(E1–E5)]
axioms.description: Context changes arise exclusively through structural adjustments in institutions, rules, and norms. The speed and scope of these changes depend on the intervention elasticity Ω(C⃗,ΔI,α_control), which describes how sensitively the context reacts to institutional impulses.

axioms.title: Salience of Context Factors
axioms.formula: Eff(C_i) = w_i · U (when S_i ≥ θ_S, else 0); σ_dyn(C_i,t) = σ_0(C_i) + ρ · dC_i/dt; Eff(C_i,t) = w_i · σ_dyn(C_i,t) · U
axioms.description: Only salient context factors are behaviorally relevant. Dynamic salience σ_dyn(C_i,t) allows time-dependent perception intensity as a function of context change.

axioms.title: Tasks as Context
axioms.formula: U(Ti) = αi*INU + βi*KNU + γi*IDN; U(S) = Σ U(Ti) + Σ δ * R(Ti,Tj|K) * min{U(Ti), U(Tj)}
axioms.description: Activities are contextual elements of human behavior and are described via standardized dimensions. Relations between tasks can be complementary, substituting, or neutral.

axioms.title: Jobs as Task Combination
axioms.formula: J = { (Ti, wi) | Σ wi = 1 }; U(J) = Σ wi*U(Ti) + Σ δ * R(Ti,Tj|K) * min{wi*U(Ti), wj*U(Tj)}
axioms.description: A job is a structured combination of task dimensions with weightings, relations, and temporal structure.

axioms.title: Teams as Coordinated Job Combination
axioms.formula: Θ = {J1, J2, …, Jn}; U(Θ) = Σ U(Jk) + Σ λ * C(Jk, Jl|K)
axioms.description: A team is a combination of individuals with different job profiles whose coordinated cooperation is necessary to fulfill a task in the required time and quality.

axioms.title: Departments as Structured Team Combination
axioms.formula: A = {Θ1, Θ2, …, Θm}; U(A) = Σ U(Θr) + Σ μ * C(Θr, Θs|K)
axioms.description: A department is a combination of multiple teams aligned toward a common goal. Utility results from team utility plus coordination effects.

axioms.title: Organizations as Coordinated Department Combination
axioms.formula: O = {A1, A2, …, Ap}; U(O) = Σ U(Aq) + Σ ν * C(Aq, Ar|K) + G(O)
axioms.description: An organization is a coordinated combination of multiple departments with shared governance, culture, and strategy.

axioms.title: Networks and Ecosystems
axioms.formula: N = {O1, O2, …, On}; U(N) = Σ U(Oi) + Σ ρ * C(Oi, Oj|K)
axioms.description: Networks emerge through cooperation of multiple organizations. They are characterized by dependencies, alliances, and shared infrastructure.

axioms.title: Societies and Markets
axioms.formula: S = {N1, N2, …, Nq}; U(S) = Σ U(Ni) + Σ σ * C(Ni, Nj|K) + I(S)
axioms.description: Societies emerge from the interaction of multiple networks and institutions. Markets are specific forms of societal coordination.

axioms.title: Multidimensionality of Rewards
axioms.formula: ΔU_Cash = α * INU; ΔU_Gift = α * INU + β * KNU + γ * IDN; ΔU_Choice = ΔU_Option + λ * (KNU + IDN)
axioms.description: Rewards that activate multiple utility axes simultaneously have stronger effects than one-dimensional rewards. Freedom of choice additionally amplifies the effect through IDN and KNU effects.

axioms.title: Freedom of Choice as Context Factor
axioms.formula: ΔU_Choice+ = ΔU_Option + λ * (KNU + IDN); ΔU_Choice- = - φ * κ_choice(n, δ); ΔU_Choice = ΔU_Option + λ * (KNU + IDN) - φ * κ_choice(n, δ)
axioms.description: Freedom of choice amplifies KNU and IDN but simultaneously increases complexity and uncertainty.

axioms.title: Degree of Institutionalization of Divergence
axioms.formula: Context_Resilience = (1 - Context_Drift) * α_control
axioms.description: Systems possess a variable capacity to absorb and maintain stable divergent perception levels (E0–E5). This capacity describes the institutional mechanism that compensates context drift and maintains coherence.

A5.title: Prerequisites and Dependencies
A5.text: Conditions: Context axes must be specified or reconstructed as vector C(t). Segment logic (BCM2_09_SEG7257) must be actively available. Connection to A_mod(t), R(t), and ΔC(t) is required. LLM-supported context extraction can be used when C⃗(t) is incomplete. Dependencies: modules 7240, 7243, 7257, 7256. Meta reference: BCM2_00_STD9232 §2.5. Status: active. Validation rule: AOM-SEM-02. Validation status: STRUCT_VALID_200. Last audit: 2025-10-24.

A6.title: Module Integration and Linkages
A6.text: Module links: Awareness (7240) - Context dependency of A_mod(t); Complementarity (7243) - Context-modulated coupling via κ(t); Segment Logic (7257) - Context influences segment reaction; Journey (7256) - Context determines transitions and stability. Integration type: operational linkage matrix. Meta reference: BCM2_00_STD9232 §2.6. Status: active. Validation rule: AOM-STRUC-02. Validation status: STRUCT_VALID_200.

A7.title: Semantic Boundaries and Limitations
A7.text: Statement: Context is not individual belief, not decision, not motivation. It is structural effect space and not substitutable by utility logic. Boundary type: semantic limit. Implication: The module may not be used to model individual preference or motivation systems. Meta reference: BCM2_00_STD9232 §2.7. Status: active. Validation rule: AOM-SEM-03. Validation status: STRUCT_VALID_200.
